en.title: US Marshals, Anna Pigeon Mysteries: Your UK Drama Fix Arrives
en.summary: US dramas are hitting UK screens, bringing critically acclaimed series to eager viewers. From neo-western action to gripping crime procedurals, there's a new binge waiting for you.
en.body:
The frustration of spotting a must-watch US drama only to find it inaccessible in the UK is a familiar pain for international fans. Fortunately, the streaming landscape is constantly evolving, with deals between US platforms and UK broadcasters like Sky and ITV ensuring that award-winning content is more readily available than ever. While release dates may not always align with those stateside, the wait is significantly shortened, allowing dedicated fans to stay on top of the latest must-see series.

This week, audiences across the pond can finally dive into the rugged world of **Yellowstone**'s latest spin-off, **Lawmen: Bass Reeves**, which sees Luke Grimes reprising his role as Kayce Dutton. The official synopsis paints a vivid picture: "Kayce and his teammates — Pete Calvin, Belle Skinner, Andrea Cruz and Miles Kittle — must balance the high psychological cost of serving as the last line of defence in the region’s war on violence with their duty to their families, which for Kayce includes his son Tate and his confidantes Mo and Thomas Rainwater from the Broken Rock reservation." This second season promises more of the signature neo-western grit that has defined Taylor Sheridan's expansive universe, offering a deep dive into the complexities of law and order in Montana. Saddle up for more cowboy action on Paramount+ starting October 5th.

## Crime Solvers Descend on UK Screens

Beyond the dusty trails of Montana, another compelling US drama makes its debut for UK viewers: the **Anna Pigeon Mysteries**. Based on Nevada Barr's best-selling novels, this crime series centers on Anna Pigeon (Tracy Spiridakos), a National Park ranger grappling with a troubled past. Seeking solace away from the city, Anna channels her personal turmoil into solving crimes that unfold within the serene yet dangerous landscapes of America's national parks. The series offers a unique blend of procedural crime-solving and character-driven drama, exploring themes of resilience and the search for peace amidst stunning natural backdrops.

## Why This Matters to Binge-Watchers

For dedicated series fans, the increased accessibility of these US dramas is a game-changer. It means less reliance on unofficial channels and a more streamlined viewing experience, allowing for full immersion into complex narratives and character arcs. The availability of shows like **Lawmen: Bass Reeves** and **Anna Pigeon Mysteries** means fans can engage with trending franchises and discover new favourites without the frustrating delays previously associated with international releases. This is particularly crucial for shows with intricate plotlines that benefit from immediate, uninterrupted viewing, fostering a stronger connection to the on-screen drama and its creators' visions.

## What's Next for US Dramas in the UK

As more streaming deals are struck, UK audiences can anticipate an even wider array of US television hitting their screens. Keep an eye on Paramount+ for further **Yellowstone** universe expansions and explore other platforms for new crime dramas and genre series. The landscape is constantly shifting, promising more compelling stories for international fans to devour.

content_raw: We've all faced the disappointment of finding a US drama we really want to watch, only for it not to be available in the UK. The US is constantly creating must-see entertainment content and you might be thinking that these programs are only available to US audiences — but that's not the case. Thanks to these US streaming platforms securing deals with UK broadcasters like Sky and ITV, we can now watch award-winning content from a variety of genres. Although the UK isn't guaranteed the same release date as those across the pond, it saves you from waiting an age until they reach UK screens. Here are the US dramas available to watch on both UK channels and streaming this week, as well as our top picks. Marshals season 2 The second season of the Yellowstone spin-off sees Luke Grimes reprise his role as former US Navy SEAL Kayce Dutton who joins an elite unit of US Marshals to bring range justice to Montana. The official synopsis reads: "Kayce and his teammates — Pete Calvin, Belle Skinner, Andrea Cruz and Miles Kittle — must balance the high psychological cost of serving as the last line of defence in the region’s war on violence with their duty to their families, which for Kayce includes his son Tate and his confidantes Mo and Thomas Rainwater from the Broken Rock reservation." Saddle up for more cowboy action in the latest chapter of Taylor Sheridan 's neo-western saga on Paramount+ on 5 October. Anna Pigeon Mysteries (Image credit: Michelle Faye/USA Network © VERSANT MEDIA 2025. All Rights Reserved) Based on Nevada Barr's best-selling novels of the same name, the crime drama follows Anna Pigeon (Tracy Spiridakos), a National Park ranger with a devastating past. After moving away from the city, Anna now channels her turmoil into solving crimes that take place within the park grounds, no matter who or what gets in her way. But as Anna tries to outrun her demons and protect the park, she discovers the greatest threat isn't the wildlife or weather, but the dark side of humanity. Anna Pigeon Mysteries airs on U&Drama on 6 October. Three Women (Image credit: Emily V Aragones/SHOWTIME.) In this adaptation of Lisa Taddeo's novel of the same name, three women each take radical steps to reclaim their lives when they tell their relationship stories to writer Gia (Shailene Woodley), who narrates their complicated personal experiences throughout the series. Three Women features an all-star cast of Betty Gilpin as Lina, who is living in deeply religious America where her husband refuses to be intimate with her anymore, DeWanda Wise as Sloan, a successful woman in a loving but open marriage, and Gabrielle Creevy as Maggie, a young woman traumatised by a relationship she had with her married high school teacher. The first three episodes debut on Channel 4 on 4 October.
